questions.text: Which statement keeps abandonment compensation source-safe?

options.text: Payment follows services already rendered and the amount due at the reached stage.
Payment is always zero if no building is completed.
Payment is always the final project construction cost.
Payment is decided only by the general contractor.

questions.rationale: SPP 202 frames abandonment as payment for rendered services at the stage reached.
questions.explanation: Inadequate; handoff requires comprehensive documentation beyond drawings. Inefficient; comprehensive handoff prevents redesign of completed work. Incorrectly treats design documentation as confidential; client owns the work product. Comprehensive handoff documentation facilitates continuity and allows the next architect to proceed efficiently. The first architect should provide complete Design Development deliverables, consultant information, and design rationale. Comprehensive handoff (drawings, specs, consultants, site data, cost estimates, program, design rationale) enables the next architect to proceed efficiently.

questions.text: Why is an owner-ordered change after approval not treated as unpaid basic work?

options.text: SPP 202 requires payment for extra time, resources, drafting, or office expenses caused by the approved-output change.
Because every design change is always free until construction starts.
Because only the contractor may charge for changes.
Because changes after approval cancel the earlier fee schedule.

questions.rationale: The source expressly makes post-approval owner changes compensable as extra time, resources, drafting, or office expenses.

questions.text: Under SPP 202, what is the source-safe fee rule when the Architect's work is abandoned or suspended in part?

options.text: The Owner pays for services rendered corresponding to the amount due at the stage reached.
All architect compensation is forfeited.
The Architect automatically receives more than 100 percent of the fee.
The building official sets the professional fee after abandonment.

questions.rationale: SPP 202 ties payment to services rendered and the stage reached when work is abandoned or suspended.

questions.text: Under the checked SPP 202 wording, what happens if suspension of construction exceeds six months?

options.text: The fee for the remaining works is doubled.
The owner-architect agreement is automatically void.
The contractor receives the Architect's fee.
All remaining services become reimbursables only.

questions.rationale: The six-month rule in the checked source doubles the fee for remaining works.

questions.text: What must an LEA answer identify before computing an abandonment-related fee consequence?

options.text: The service stage reached at suspension or abandonment.
The contractor's preferred construction method.
The date of PRC registration renewal.
The number of bidders invited to tender.

questions.rationale: The source-safe calculation starts with the amount due at the stage of suspension or abandonment.

questions.text: A client approves drawings, then asks for a different layout before permit filing. Which cost category does SPP 202 support?

options.text: Additional payment for extra time, resources, drafting, or other office expenses.
A free revision because the project has not been built.
A payment bond claim against subcontractors.
A public bidding addendum only.

questions.rationale: Post-approval owner-ordered changes are separately compensable under the checked source.

questions.text: Which fact distinguishes non-implementation compensation from ordinary early-stage abandonment?

options.text: The Architect has prepared the plans, designs, specifications, and construction documents that SPP 202 treats as ninety percent of the work.
The contractor has posted a guarantee bond.
The owner has hired a resident inspector.
The project is located within 50 kilometers of the office.

questions.rationale: The non-implementation rule turns on completed plans and documents, not on contractor bond or travel-distance facts.

questions.text: What is unsafe in an answer about fees for abandoned projects?

options.text: Claiming a full or punitive fee without checking the reached stage and source condition.
Using the stage reached to determine compensation.
Recognizing the ninety-percent non-implementation rule for completed plans and documents.
Separating post-approval changes from basic work.

questions.rationale: The source supports stage-based compensation and specific conditions; it does not create a blanket punitive fee.

questions.text: If the Owner does not implement plans and contract documents prepared by the Architect, what compensation does the checked SPP 202 source support?

options.text: Compensation corresponding to ninety percent of the Architect's fee.
No compensation because no contractor started work.
A fixed five percent fee regardless of the stage reached.
A doubled full fee without reference to construction suspension.

questions.rationale: The checked source states that completed detailed design and contract documents represent ninety percent of the Architect's work, and non-implementation supports that corresponding compensation.

questions.text: When construction is carried out in different periods and the Architect's construction-phase burden increases, what happens to construction-phase charges?

options.text: They are adjusted proportionately for the services rendered during the construction phase.
They are automatically erased.
They become a contractor bond premium.
They become a fixed honorarium unrelated to remaining work.

questions.rationale: SPP 202 states that construction-phase charges are adjusted proportionately when different construction periods increase the Architect's burden.
